question.text: Given the sets $A = \{o,p,q,r \}$ and $B = \{ q,r,v,w \},$ find $A \cup B.$
question.explanation:
The union $A \cup B$ consists of all the elements that are in either $A$ or $B,$ or both. To represent $A \cup B,$ we will shade in all the area that is contained in either $A$ or $B,$ or both.

The elements $o,p,q,r,v,w$ are in either $A$ or $B$, or both. Therefore, the union of $A$ and $B$ is

\[ A \cup B = \{ o,p,q,r,v,w \}. \]

exampleAnswers.title: Finding Unions of Sets Given Verbally

question.text: Let $X$ and $Y$ be the set of all non-negative integer powers of $3$ and the set of all multiples of $4$ greater than $0,$ respectively. What is $X\cup Y?$
question.explanation:
The non-negative integer powers of $3$ are

\[ X = \{ 1,3,9,27,\ldots \}. \]

Likewise, multiples of $4$ that are greater than $0$ are

\[ Y = \{ 4,8,12,16,20,24,\ldots \}. \]

Now, $X \cup Y$ is the union of $X$ and $Y,$ which means that we want to find the elements that are in either $X$ or $Y,$ or both. In other words, $X\cup Y$ denotes the set of natural numbers that are either powers of $3$ or multiples of $4.$

\[ \begin{align*} X \cup Y &= \{ 1,3,9,27,\ldots \} \cup \{ 4,8,12,16,20,24,\ldots \} \\[3pt] &= \{ 1,3,4,8,9,12,16,20,24,27,\ldots \}. \end{align*} \]

question.text: Let $A$ and $B$ be the set of all multiples of $4$ greater than $0$ and the set of all multiples of $5$ greater than $0,$ respectively. What is $A\cup B?$
question.explanation:
The multiples of $4$ that are greater than $0$ are

\[ A = \{ 4,8,12,16,20,\ldots \}. \]

Likewise, multiples of $5$ that are greater than $0$ are

\[ B = \{ 5,10,15,20,\ldots \}. \]

Now, $A \cup B$ is the union of $A$ and $B,$ which means that we want to find the elements that are in either $A$ or $B,$ or both. In other words, $A\cup B$ denotes the set of natural numbers that are either multiple of $4$ or multiple of $5.$ So, we have

\[ \begin{align*} A \cup B &= \{ 4,8,12,16,20,\ldots \} \cup \{ 5,10,15,20, \ldots \} \\[3pt] &= \{ 4,5,8,10,12,15,16,20,\ldots \}. \end{align*} \]
